messages:
elaine: quick proposal — we want a repeatable soft-cutover playbook + customer crediting program to incent migrations off pinned legacy models. goal: reduce risk, buy goodwill, and validate telemetry gating before hard retire. doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/migration-credits (WIP)
elaine: key pieces: 1) cohort definition + canary plan, 2) credit tiering & billing flow, 3) acceptance gates (quality + infra), 4) legal/data residency checks, 5) rollback & rollback-credits policy
samir: +1 on cohorting. question: how do we actually apply credits? one-off invoice credit or token-based? need to avoid double-billing edge cases for committed seats.
maria: from CS perspective customers expect a single-line credit on next invoice. token-based systems are fine for self-serve but enterprise contracts will demand invoice credits + amendment note. also need language for 'non-refundable' credits if they cancel mid-migration.
dillon: on acceptance gates — suggest we make them telemetry-only for canary (latency p50/p95, error rate, and quality delta on our eval set). if metrics stable for N days, promote cohort. otherwise rollback automatically and apply a remediation plan.
kavya: suggested credit tiers in doc (small: $2k, mid: $10k, large: $50k) based on spend and migration effort. propose credits vest over 30 days to avoid gaming.
elaine: @samir good call — let's support both paths: invoice credit for enterprise + token credit for self-serve. include idempotency key and ledger event so billing-bot can reconcile. billing-bot: will emit a webhook to accounting when credit applied.
billing-bot: noted — need final approval code and contract id to post credit. also recommend a `migration_credit_reason` audit field.
maria: legal will want a standardized amendment template. can someone draft? i can loop in compliance for residency checks (some customers require changes only in-region).
samir: on the telemetry gating, what's the eval set? are we using customer prompts or Redwood canonical prompt bundle? using customer prompts is more accurate but raises data privacy concerns.
dillon: run both. keep the canonical prompt bundle as the gating baseline; for customers who opt-in we can run a private diff on their sanitized prompts (opt-in only). that meets privacy while catching regressions.
kavya: can we automate partial rollback credits? e.g., if quality drops but infra fine, give a 50% credit + remediation window. avoids full rollback churn.
maria: customers will like that. but legal needs to sign off on partial credits as it's effectively a service level concession.
elaine: operations: what does the cutover playbook look like? quick sketch in doc but here's a mini-runbook: 
```
- Day 0: announce window to customer + create canary cohort (1% traffic)
- Day 1-3: monitor telemetry, run eval set, review daily with CS
- Day 4: if gates pass -> ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% over 72 hrs
- If quality delta > threshold at any ramp -> pause, rollback to previous model, trigger credit workflow
- After 7 days at 100% stable -> close migration, post final invoice credit
```
elaine: want to add a mandatory 'preflight' that checks model compatibility (tokenization, special tokens) and quantization path to avoid silent failures.
samir: also add an infra-cost floor: if a customer forces a very large canary that spikes GPU cost we should have a cost-sharing clause. maybe bill excess separately.
kavya: operationally, CS will own the credit negotiation; billing will own execution; product owns gating & rollout. need an owner for the playbook doc (I can shepherd).
maria: I'll prepare an amendment template and list of customers with residency restrictions.
dillon: for automation — propose a `catalog-migration` job that wires metrics -> alerting -> canary-promote API. if thresholds breach, it triggers `billing-bot apply-credit --type partial --amount 0.5x` (example).
billing-bot: stub CLI accepted, but we need an auditable event id returned to CS so customers can reference it.
elaine: next steps: @kavya draft credit tiers + vesting rules; @samir spec invoice vs token API + idempotency; @dillon spec telemetry thresholds + eval bundle; @maria legal template + residency list. I'll schedule a 30m sync Friday. any objections?
kavya: none — i'll start a tracking spreadsheet and add sample math for ROI. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
samir: no objections. will include example webhook payloads in the spec.
maria: fine. looping in legal after your draft, @kavya.
dillon: i'll prototype canary-promote API by EOD Thursday.
elaine: awesome. thanks team — aim to have a near-final playbook before EOW. please put comments in the doc, not the thread. :thumbsup:
